_note: This file provides question topics and stems for quiz generation. It is NOT a quiz. AI agents generating lessons read this file to decide what to test — they must write original questions using the vocabulary and grammar in the Knowledge Package.

assessmentTopics: Extended family vocabulary (grandparents, uncle, aunt, cousin, niece, nephew)
Describing physical appearance using adjectives (curly, straight, wavy, bald, freckles, dimples)
Present perfect with 'just' to describe recent actions
questionStems: Your mother's brother is your ___.
Your aunt's daughter is your ___.
Which word describes hair that is tightly coiled?
Complete: 'She has ___ hair.' (small marks on skin)
Complete: 'He has just ___ his homework.' (present perfect)
'They have just ___ lunch.' — which verb form is correct?
Which sentence uses 'just' correctly with present perfect?
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'nephew'?
True or false: 'dimples' are marks on the face when you smile.
Fill in: 'My father's sister is my ___.'
Which adjective describes hair that is not straight and not curly — somewhere in between?
Complete: 'She ___ just arrived.' (has/have)

assessmentTopics: Natural world vocabulary (waterfall, glacier, cave, volcano, canyon, rainforest)
Describing geographical features
Present perfect with 'ever' and 'never' for experiences
questionStems: A ___ is a large mass of ice that moves slowly.
Which natural feature is formed when water falls from a high place?
Complete: 'Have you ___ visited a volcano?' (ever/never)
'I have ___ seen a glacier.' — which word completes this negative sentence?
Which sentence correctly asks about experience with 'ever'?
True or false: A canyon is a deep valley with steep sides.
Fill in: 'She has ___ been to a rainforest.' (never)
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'waterfall'?
Which of these is found underground? (cave / rainforest / glacier / volcano)
Complete: '___ you ever climbed a mountain?' (Have/Has)
Which geographical feature is most associated with lava?
True or false: 'ever' is used in negative sentences.

assessmentTopics: Household chores and responsibilities (vacuum, mow the lawn, take out the trash, wash up)
Obligations with 'have to' and 'don't have to'
Advice with 'should' and 'shouldn't'
questionStems: Complete: 'You ___ to vacuum the living room every week.' (have/has)
Which sentence shows something is NOT necessary?
You ___ eat too much sugar. (shouldn't/should)
Fill in: 'She doesn't ___ to cook dinner tonight.' (have)
True or false: 'should' means the same as 'must'.
Which chore involves cutting grass outside?
Complete: 'We ___ take out the trash on Mondays.' (have to)
What does 'wash up' mean? (wash the dishes / wash your hair / wash the car)
You look tired. You ___ go to bed earlier. (should/shouldn't)
Fill in: 'He ___ have to wear a uniform at home.' (doesn't/don't)
Which word means to clean a floor using a machine?
True or false: 'have to' expresses obligation.

assessmentTopics: Countable and uncountable nouns (rice, bread, apple, egg)
Using 'some' and 'any' correctly
Food vocabulary and nutrition
questionStems: Is 'rice' countable or uncountable?
Complete: 'There is ___ milk in the fridge.' (some/any)
Complete: 'Are there ___ apples left?' (some/any)
Which word is uncountable? (egg / water / orange / sandwich)
True or false: We use 'any' in negative sentences.
Fill in: 'She doesn't have ___ sugar.' (some/any)
Complete: 'I need ___ bread for the sandwich.' (some/any)
Which sentence is correct? (There is some rice. / There is any rice.)
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'uncountable'?
True or false: 'some' is used in questions to offer something.
Fill in: 'Do you have ___ homework tonight?' (some/any)
Which food is countable? (water / juice / cookie / salt)

assessmentTopics: School and public rules vocabulary
Prohibition and obligation with 'must' and 'mustn't'
Difference between 'must' and 'have to'
questionStems: Complete: 'You ___ run in the corridors.' (must/mustn't)
Which word shows something is prohibited?
True or false: 'must' and 'mustn't' are opposites.
Fill in: 'Students ___ wear their school uniform.' (must)
Complete: 'You ___ talk during the exam.' (mustn't)
Which sentence is a rule? Choose the one with 'must'.
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'prohibited'?
True or false: 'mustn't' means 'it is not necessary'.
Fill in: 'You ___ drop litter in the park.' (mustn't)
Complete: 'Visitors ___ show their ID cards.' (must)
Which word describes an official rule that must be followed?
In which place would you most likely see the rule 'You must be quiet'?

assessmentTopics: Future predictions and plans with 'will' and 'won't'
Technology and future vocabulary (robot, solar panel, electric car, renewable energy)
Making predictions about the future
questionStems: Complete: 'In the future, cars ___ use petrol.' (will/won't — negative prediction)
Which sentence makes a positive prediction about the future?
True or false: 'won't' is the short form of 'will not'.
Fill in: 'Scientists think robots ___ do most jobs.' (will)
Complete: 'People ___ live on the moon one day.' (will/won't)
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'renewable energy'?
Which technology uses the sun to make electricity?
True or false: Electric cars use petrol.
Fill in: 'I think it ___ rain tomorrow.' (will)
Complete: 'She ___ be late — she left early.' (won't)
Which word describes energy sources that don't run out?
In which sentence is 'will' used for a spontaneous decision?

assessmentTopics: Jobs and community helpers vocabulary (paramedic, firefighter, surgeon, architect, journalist)
Defining relative clauses with 'who', 'which', and 'that'
Describing people and things using relative clauses
questionStems: Complete: 'A paramedic is someone ___ gives emergency medical treatment.' (who/which)
Complete: 'That is the building ___ was designed by a famous architect.' (who/which/that)
True or false: We use 'who' for people and 'which' for things.
Fill in: 'She is the journalist ___ wrote that article.' (who/that)
Complete: 'A surgeon is a doctor ___ performs operations.' (who)
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'paramedic'?
Which word can replace both 'who' and 'which' in a relative clause?
True or false: 'that' can only be used for things, not people.
Fill in: 'This is the machine ___ prints the newspaper.' (which/that)
Complete: 'The firefighter ___ rescued the child received an award.' (who/that)
Which job involves designing buildings?
What does a journalist do? (report news / fight fires / perform surgery / design buildings)

assessmentTopics: Festival and celebration vocabulary (carnival, fireworks, costume, parade, lantern, feast)
Review of all grammar structures from Units 1–8
Describing celebrations and cultural events
questionStems: Which word describes a large public celebration with music and dancing in the streets?
Complete: 'People wear ___ at costume parties.' (costumes/carnivals)
True or false: Fireworks are usually displayed during daytime celebrations.
Fill in: 'The festival ___ just started.' (has/have — present perfect)
Complete: 'You ___ miss the lantern festival — it's beautiful!' (shouldn't)
What is the Vietnamese meaning of 'feast'?
Which sentence uses a relative clause correctly to describe a festival?
Complete: 'There will ___ be fireworks tonight.' (will/won't — affirmative)
True or false: A parade is a procession of people moving through a public place.
Fill in: 'Have you ___ attended a carnival?' (ever)
Which celebration is most associated with lanterns in Vietnamese culture?
Complete: 'She has ___ prepared the feast.' (just)
